stages.title: Scarcity
stages.sub: Why every economy has to choose: limited resources against unlimited wants.

stages.name: Opportunity cost

steps.q: Scarcity means not everyone can have everything. So what must people, firms and governments do?
steps.wrong: Wait until there is enough for everyone
steps.hint: If everything cannot be had at once, what is left to do?

steps.q: When you choose one option, do you still get the ones you did not choose?
steps.hint: You chose the phone. Can you also spend that same money on the holiday?

steps.q: Can the same land, workers and machines be used to make something else instead?
steps.hint: Could the bottling factory make juice or fizzy drinks with the very same resources?

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 3 key terms into the two chains that lead to one concept. Chain 1 is what choosing involves. Chain 2 is what resources can do.

steps.q: Of everything you gave up, which one do you count when judging a choice?
steps.right: The best one you gave up
steps.hint: You can only have one thing instead. Which of the things you gave up would you actually have picked?

steps.q: So what is the real cost of a choice?
steps.right: The value of the next best alternative you gave up
steps.hint: Money is only one way of counting. What did you actually give up?

stages.title: Opportunity cost
stages.sub: The real cost of any choice, measured by what you give up.
